To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the extracellular matrix protein crosslinking enzyme tissue transglutamine (tTG) is expressed in the extracellular matrix during maturation of rat lung parenchymal tissues.
tissue transglutamine (tTG) is expressed and externalised into the extracellular matrices of lung shortly before the maturation of an area of an organ.
the enzyme product of tissue transglutinase (tTG), gamma-glutamylepsilon-lysine-crosslinks, and extracellular tTg appear in the rat lung shortly before maturing of the organ area.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether tTG may be involved in the stabilization of extracellular components during lung development.
the role of tissue tTG in the maturation of the lung.
the role of tissue tTG as a regulator of the maturation of the extracellular matrix in developing lung.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tTG is involved in the maturation of the lung.
tTG is involved in the maturation process of the lung.
tTG may be involved in the maturation process of lung tissue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tTG may play an important role in the maturation of the lung.
tTG is involved in the maturation of lung parenchymal basement membrane and microfibrillar components.
tTG is involved in the maturation of the extracellular matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tTG plays an essential role in the maturation of the extracellular matrix in mammalian organs, including lung.
the lung matures in a stepwise fashion and that the maturation is accompanied by a stepwise expression of extracellular tTG.
the enzyme product (the cross-link) and extracellular tissue transglutamase are present in the developing lung parenchymal tissue at the time of alveolarization.
